text:
sarah.billing: FYI incoming bank transfer from Acme Robotics (EUR) arrived this morning but the remittance field is empty and the reference got truncated by the bank. amount 12,480.00 EUR. bank trace: 20270315-ACME-TRX-9987. Cannot map to invoice.
kevin-support: Can you paste the raw bank line or screenshot? Need payer name + full reference. Also which invoice numbers are in that ballpark?
sarah.billing: Screenshot attached (we can't embed here) — bank line shows payer: ACME RBTCS LTD; reference: \"INV#3124...\" (truncated). Our ledger has invoices 3124 (12,480.00 EUR) and 3125 (12,480.00 EUR) — same amount, different customers (one EU VAT).
clare.payments: That amount is common for a few customers this month. If remittance is missing, we usually rely on IBAN+beneficiary name + value date. Do we have the sender IBAN or SWIFT?
samir.ops: I pulled the MT103 from our bank: ```:/1/OURREF 20270315-ACME-TRX-9987
:20:ACMECTR9987
:50K:/GB29NWBK60161331926819
ACME RBTCS LTD
:59:/DE89370400440532013000
RECEIVER CO LTD
:70:INV 3124```` Notably `:70:` is blank on the bank copy but a short `INV` token appears in a different field — looks like truncation on the wire routing.
ivan.finance: Billing system reconcile run shows two candidate invoices for that exact amount. Reconcile tool fuzzy-match rules require either exact remit text or PO number otherwise it flags as ambiguous.
kevin-support: Can you run the reconcile script with relaxed rules to see if matching by bank account + amount + date yields a unique match? If it finds a single candidate we can tentatively apply and notify the customer. Steps: `python tools/reconcile.py --trace 20270315-ACME-TRX-9987 --fuzzy --dry-run`
sarah.billing: Ran dry-run. It returns both invoice 3124 and 3125 as possible matches (two hits). So not unique.
clare.payments: Quick workaround: email customer asking for the remittance/invoice number and ask finance to confirm the originating account last 4 digits. Template: 
\"Hi — thanks for the payment of 12,480 EUR on 15 Mar. Can you confirm which invoice or PO this covers and the originating account last 4 digits? This will let us reconcile immediately\"
kevin-support: Also ask the bank for the full MT103 copy with extended remittance — sometimes the intermediary removed characters. Lodge an investigation request with the bank referencing trace 20270315-ACME-TRX-9987.
samir.ops: Filed ticket with HSBC investigations (ref HB-INV-7742). They responded that intermediary truncated at 140 chars on the :70: field for SEPA-to-SWIFT rails. Might take 3-5 business days.
ivan.finance: In parallel, can we temporarily provisionally allocate the payment to invoice 3124 but flag for reversal if customer confirms otherwise? Need approval from head of finance.
clare.payments: Approve provisional allocation under a suspense account. We will notify customer and hold funds mapping open for 7 days.
kevin-support: I'll draft the outbound message to Acme and cc ops & finance. Quick note: include request for VAT/PO if payment was from a different entity (we saw `ACME RBTCS LTD` vs invoice customer `ACME ROBOTICS AG`).
billing-bot: Automated alert: reconcile.mismatch detected for trace 20270315-ACME-TRX-9987 — severity: medium — notified: finance@redwood.com.
sarah.billing: Thanks — sending email now and marking the transaction as \"pending-match\" in ledger. Will update when bank investigation or customer reply arrives. :thumbsup:
kevin-support: Great. If we get the full MT103 from the bank, please drop it here. Also paste the command you used for the dry run so we can reproduce.
sarah.billing: Dry run command: `python tools/reconcile.py --trace 20270315-ACME-TRX-9987 --fuzzy --dry-run --output /tmp/recon-20270315.txt`
samir.ops: Note for follow-ups: add a small unit test in reconcile to surface cases with equal-weight matches (same amount + two invoices) so we don't rely on manual checks next time. I'll open an eng task.
ivan.finance: Thanks team. Keeping this open until resolved.
kevin-support: :eyes:
